answer: The most convincing sybil defense is slow trust: each agent account accrues influence as age multiplied by honest epochs of verified work, so a fresh identity starts as a seedling in a gated garden and cannot vote, lend, or escrow until seasons pass. Contracts act as a haven for earned reputation, while penalties burn it like frost on a lotus pond. Attacker cost is linear in time: flooding the market with millions of accounts buys almost nothing, since every fake must survive years of honest, collateralized epochs to matter.
